name: Do I need a permit for cabinet refacing in San Diego, Chula Vista, or Coronado?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for cabinet refacing in San Diego, Chula Vista, or Coronado?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Permit needs depend on the work, property, and jurisdiction—not simply on the word “refacing.” In the City of San Diego, limited cabinet or countertop work may fall under published no-plan categories in certain residential buildings, while plumbing, electrical, structural, historic-resource, or other alterations may require additional review.

Context: Requirements can differ in Chula Vista, Coronado, National City, Imperial Beach, and other San Diego County communities. Cosmetic surface work is not the same as relocating cabinets, changing a sink, adding circuits, or altering walls.

Key factors:
- Whether cabinet locations, countertops, plumbing, gas, or electrical systems change.
- Whether the home is historic or in a designated historic district.
- Which city or unincorporated area has authority over the property.

Practical guidance: Provide the exact address and full scope before work is scheduled, and ask who will confirm permit requirements. Keep approvals and inspection records with the project documents.

Elite Remodeling & Design’s design-build process includes permit coordination when the project scope calls for it.
acceptedAnswer.description: A purely cosmetic refacing job may not need the same approvals as work that relocates cabinets or changes plumbing, gas, electrical, walls, or historic features. Rules vary by jurisdiction; provide the property address and complete scope so requirements can be confirmed before work starts.
